recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No HL7/fhir source follow-up is needed for FHIR-25424 unless a future validator/tooling repository audit shows the same bug remains in current validator code.
issue_request: FHIR-25424 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction raised against R4 terminologies. It reported that the validator rejected a CodeableConcept with multiple Codings even though one Coding was in the required value set, and expected that instance to pass because required binding only requires one Coding value from the specified value set.
initial_application: No HL7/fhir commit mentioning FHIR-25424 was found. The terminology wording the issue relied on predates the issue: commit bd75ca84005d97a15b506fab3de25925bed9cf02, #9672, made binding requirements clearer in 2016 and added the CodeableConcept rule that one Coding value SHALL be from the specified value set.
additional_context: The current build-scope source/terminologies.html page still contains the expected CodeableConcept required-binding rule. FHIR-I minutes from 2020-01-13 classify FHIR-25424 as a validator problem and core-tooling technical correction, and the referenced Zulip thread records Lloyd calling the behavior a validator error and Grahame saying it was fixed in the next release. No validator implementation source was found in this HL7/fhir checkout.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No source hunk was necessary because the current spec source is already correct and the actual fix belongs to validator/tooling code outside this repository.
